episode_title: Connecting the Systems Behind the Sales Process with Andy Janaitis

real_qa.q: Why do manufacturers get three different answers when asking about their quote win rate in one company?
real_qa.r: The issue stems from disconnected systems and lack of data standardization. In smaller manufacturers in the two to twenty million dollar revenue band, sales processes are often founder-driven and data isn't being properly recorded into systems as they should be used. Different departments or people have different ideas about what the metric means, and when systems aren't connected, the same question can be answered from different data sources, none of which are actionable.
real_qa.requete: why three answers quote win rate

real_qa.q: What is the first problem Andy Janaitis fixes when working with manufacturers?
real_qa.r: The first thing to fix is where data gets captured and ensuring systems are connected so nobody has to retype records. Once systems are standardized and connected, you can build reports that show how the business is running in real time, then address the biggest bottleneck those numbers point out.
real_qa.requete: Janaitis Business Systems first fix data capture

real_qa.q: How can manufacturers enforce correct sales process behavior through system design rather than just documentation?
real_qa.r: Rather than writing SOPs that nobody reads, systems should be designed such that you cannot break process. Andy uses industrial engineering principles: make the system work only if the correct process is followed. This is the poke-yoke approach—designing systems that force compliance, similar to how RFID scanners could prevent material access unless tags were scanned, ensuring behavior change through system constraint rather than voluntary adherence.
real_qa.requete: poke-yoke sales process system design force compliance

real_qa.q: What guarantee does Janaitis Business Systems offer on project implementation timelines?
real_qa.r: Andy guarantees the build in 90 days or works free until it ships. He does not rip out what you're running, does not run AI pilots that collect dust, and commits to delivering the system integration within the guaranteed timeframe or continues work at no charge.

real_qa.q: Why do small manufacturers run their business by rule of thumb instead of using data-driven KPI trees?
real_qa.r: The main reason is that it takes too long to create the reports needed to pull the data they really need. Creating manual KPI trees and dashboards is time-consuming, so owners resort to gut feel. The solution is connecting systems and automating the processes to get real-time data into dashboards instead of requiring months of manual analysis.
real_qa.requete: manufacturers KPI trees data reporting challenge
